title: Ubisoft Montreal 员工发起集体行动以保留混合办公制度
content:
Ubisoft Montreal employees rally to preserve hybrid work
Production
Business
Ubisoft Montreal employees launch collective action to preserve hybrid work schedule
A petition is the first action.
Nicole Carpenter
,
Contributor
,
Game Developer
September 30, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via Ubisoft
Ubisoft Montreal workers in the Ubisoft Workers of Montreal union have started a petition "to preserve hybrid work,"
according to a statement posted on GWU Montreal social media
. As of Wednesday, the petition has reached
more than 300 signatures from Ubisoft employees
. Many of the signatures were collected in person, GWU Montreal said.
"Today marks the public launch of the Ubisoft Workers of Montreal (UWM) campaign, with a first action: a petition to preserve hybrid work," GWU posted. "Every Ubisoft Montreal employee is invited to sign the petition and every supporter encouraged to reach out to their network to encourage them to sign!"
Ubisoft announced in January
that it was calling all employees to return to the office five days per week. It also said it was enacting layoffs, delays, and studio closures. Ubisoft, at that time, had just secured a $1.25 billion investment from Tencent. The "rightsizing" was intended to "reclaim [Ubisoft's] creative leadership, regain agility and drive sharp rebound." Ubisoft said in its January press release that the return to office policy was intended to encourage collaboration.
Related:
'We were constantly overshooting our capacity:' Arc Raiders exec says success resulted in burnout
Ubisoft's Paris-based employees
went on strike shortly
after the announcement to protest the policy.
When Ubisoft Montreal team lead David Michaud-Cromp commented publicly on the policy—
suggesting there may be another reason other than productivity for the layoffs
—Ubisoft put the veteran employee on unpaid leave. He was fired a week later. Ubisoft said in a statement to Game Developer that "sharing feedback or opinions respectfully does not lead to a dismissal."
It continued: "We have a clear Code of Conduct that outlines our shared expectations for working together safely and respectfully, which employees review and sign each year. When that is breached, our established procedures apply, including an escalation of measures depending on the nature, severity and repetition of the breach."
GWU Montreal is instructing Ubisoft workers
interested in signing the petition to do so in person
by "meet[ing] your colleagues during [break] hours".
Update 9/30:
A previous version of this story mistakenly stated that GWU Montreal was urging employees to meet colleagues during "work hours." It has been updated to accurately state that they are being urged to meet during "break hours."
